fact.en: Hydrogen makes up about 75% of all normal matter in the universe.
fact.zh: 氢约占宇宙中所有普通物质的75%。

ety.en: Named because it makes water when it burns.
ety.zh: 因燃烧时会生成水而得名。

sen.us: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
sen.uk: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
sen.zh: 水由氢和氧组成。

fact.en: Helium was first spotted as an unknown yellow line in sunlight during a solar eclipse in 1868.
fact.zh: 1868年日食期间，人们在阳光中首次发现了氦的未知黄色谱线。

ety.en: Named by Norman Lockyer after the Sun, where its line was first seen
ety.zh: 由洛克耶以太阳命名，因其谱线最早在阳光中被发现

sen.us: We filled the party balloons with helium this morning.
sen.uk: We filled the party balloons with helium this morning.
sen.zh: 今天早上我们给派对气球充了氦气。

fact.en: Batteries use more than three-quarters of all the lithium produced.
fact.zh: 全球超过四分之三的锂被用来制造电池。

ety.en: From Greek lithos, 'stone', because it was found in a solid mineral.
ety.zh: 源自希腊语lithos，意为“石头”，因发现于矿石中。

sen.us: My phone has a lithium battery inside.
sen.uk: My phone has a lithium battery inside.
sen.zh: 我的手机里有一块锂电池。

traps.why_en: The th is /θ/ (tongue between teeth), not /s/: LITH-ee-um.
traps.why_zh: th要读成咬舌音/θ/，不能读成/s/。

fact.en: Tools made of beryllium copper don't make sparks when they hit steel.
fact.zh: 铍铜合金工具撞击钢铁时不会产生火花。

ety.en: Named after beryl, the gem mineral it was first taken from.
ety.zh: 得名于绿柱石（beryl），最初从这种矿物中分离出来。

sen.us: Emeralds and aquamarines both contain beryllium.
sen.uk: Emeralds and aquamarines both contain beryllium.
sen.zh: 祖母绿和海蓝宝石都含有铍。

traps.why_en: The stress is on the second syllable: buh-RIL-ee-um.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第二个音节，不在第一个音节。

fact.en: Crystalline boron is silvery to black and extremely hard: 9.3 on the Mohs scale.
fact.zh: 晶体硼呈银色到黑色，极其坚硬，莫氏硬度达9.3。

ety.en: Coined from borax, the mineral it was isolated from, by analogy with carbon
ety.zh: 由硼砂（borax）一词仿照碳（carbon）造出，硼从硼砂中分离而来

sen.us: Our teacher showed us a small piece of boron today.
sen.uk: Our teacher showed us a small piece of boron today.
sen.zh: 今天老师给我们看了一小块硼。

fact.en: In 1772, Antoine Lavoisier showed that diamonds are a form of carbon.
fact.zh: 1772年，拉瓦锡证明了钻石是碳的一种形态。

ety.en: From Latin carbo, 'coal and charcoal'
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 carbo，意为“煤和木炭”。

sen.us: Diamonds and pencil lead are both made of carbon.
sen.uk: Diamonds and pencil lead are both made of carbon.
sen.zh: 钻石和铅笔芯都是由碳构成的。

traps.why_en: The second syllable is weak and sounds like 'bun' (KAR-bən), not a full 'bon'.
traps.why_zh: 第二个音节要弱读成 /bən/，不要读成饱满的“棒”。

fact.en: About 3% of your body's mass is nitrogen, the fourth most common element in the body.
fact.zh: 人体质量中约3%是氮，是人体含量第四多的元素。

ety.en: From French nitre, 'saltpetre', plus the French suffix -gène, 'producing'
ety.zh: 源自法语 nitre（硝石）加法语后缀 -gène（“产生”）

sen.us: Most of the air we breathe is nitrogen.
sen.uk: Most of the air we breathe is nitrogen.
sen.zh: 我们呼吸的空气大部分是氮气。

traps.why_en: The first i sounds like 'eye' (NY-truh-jun), and the last syllable is a weak 'jun', not a full 'gen'.
traps.why_zh: 首个 i 读作“爱”音，结尾 -gen 弱读为 /dʒən/，不要读成饱满的“根”。

traps.why_en: The g before e is a soft /dʒ/ sound, like in 'gentle', not a hard g.
traps.why_zh: e 前的 g 读软音 /dʒ/，像 gentle 里的 g，不读硬音 /g/。

fact.en: Oxygen makes up 88.8% of the mass of the world's oceans.
fact.zh: 按质量计，世界海洋的88.8%是氧。

ety.en: From Greek oxys, 'sharp, acid', + -genes, 'producer'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 oxys（“酸、尖锐”）+ -genes（“产生者”）

sen.us: Plants give off oxygen when sunlight shines on their leaves.
sen.uk: Plants give off oxygen when sunlight shines on their leaves.
sen.zh: 阳光照在叶子上时，植物会释放氧气。

fact.en: Fluorine was so dangerous to separate that several early chemists died or were hurt trying.
fact.zh: 氟极难分离，好几位早期化学家因此受伤甚至丧命。

ety.en: Named after the mineral fluorite, from Latin fluo; fluorite helped metal ores melt
ety.zh: 得名于萤石，源自拉丁语 fluo；萤石能帮助矿石熔化

sen.us: Fluorine compounds in toothpaste help protect your teeth.
sen.uk: Fluorine compounds in toothpaste help protect your teeth.
sen.zh: 牙膏里的氟化合物有助于保护牙齿。

traps.why_en: The 'uo' is one sound, so the word has two syllables with stress first: FLOOR-een.
traps.why_zh: uo 只发一个音，全词两个音节，重音在前：FLOOR-een。

fact.en: A balloon filled with neon will rise in air, but more slowly than a helium balloon.
fact.zh: 充满氖气的气球会在空气中上升，但比氦气球升得慢。

ety.en: From Greek neon (νέον), a form of neos, meaning 'new'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 νέον（neon），意为"新的"

sen.us: The shop sign glows with bright red neon at night.
sen.uk: The shop sign glows with bright red neon at night.
sen.zh: 这家店的招牌夜里亮着明亮的红色霓虹灯光。

fact.en: Seawater holds an estimated 10.8 grams of sodium in every liter.
fact.zh: 据估计，每升海水中含有约10.8克钠。

ety.en: Thought to come from Arabic suda, meaning 'headache'
ety.zh: 一般认为源自阿拉伯语 suda，意为“头痛”

sen.us: This soup has too much sodium for my diet.
sen.uk: This soup has too much sodium for my diet.
sen.zh: 这碗汤的钠含量对我的饮食来说太高了。

traps.why_en: The symbol Na comes from the Latin name natrium, but in English the element is called SOH-dee-um.
traps.why_zh: 符号 Na 来自拉丁名 natrium，但英语里这个元素读作 SOH-dee-um。

fact.en: In 1618, cows at Epsom in England refused a farmer's well water because of its bitter taste.
fact.zh: 1618年，英国埃普瑟姆的奶牛因井水味苦而拒绝饮用。

ety.en: From Greek, for places linked to the Magnetes tribe: Magnesia in Thessaly or Magnesia ad Sipylum
ety.zh: 源自希腊语，指马格尼特人相关地名：色萨利的马格尼西亚或锡皮洛斯的马格尼西亚

sen.us: Magnesium burns with a bright white light in science class.
sen.uk: Magnesium burns with a bright white light in science class.
sen.zh: 在科学课上，镁燃烧时发出明亮的白光。

traps.why_en: Magnesium looks like manganese, so learners often mix up the two names.
traps.why_zh: magnesium 和 manganese 拼写相近，学习者常把两个名字混淆。

traps.why_en: The 's' here sounds like /z/, so say mag-NEE-zee-um, not with a hard /s/.
traps.why_zh: 这里的 s 读 /z/，应读 mag-NEE-zee-um，不要读成清音 /s/。

fact.en: It was once so rare and hard to make that it cost more than gold.
fact.zh: 它曾经稀少又难以制取，价格比黄金还贵。

ety.en: From Latin alumen, 'alum', the mineral it was first collected from
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 alumen，意为“明矾”，最初从这种矿物中提取。

sen.us: We wrapped the sandwiches in aluminum foil for the picnic.
sen.uk: We wrapped the sandwiches in aluminium foil for the picnic.
sen.zh: 我们用铝箔把三明治包好，带去野餐。

traps.why_en: Learners mix the two versions: US is a-LOO-mi-num (4 syllables), UK is al-yoo-MIN-ee-um (5 syllables).
traps.why_zh: 学习者常把两种读法混在一起：美式重音在 LOO，共四个音节；英式重音在 MIN，共五个音节。

fact.en: Silicon makes up 27.2% of Earth's crust by weight, second only to oxygen.
fact.zh: 硅占地壳重量的27.2%，仅次于氧。

sen.us: The chip inside my phone is made from silicon.
sen.uk: The chip inside my phone is made from silicon.
sen.zh: 我手机里的芯片是用硅做的。

traps.why_en: The last syllable is weak, like 'kun' (SIL-ih-kun), not a full 'con'.
traps.why_zh: 最后一个音节要弱读成/kən/，不要读成饱满的“康”。

fact.en: An estimated two-thirds of the world's exploitable phosphate reserves are in Morocco alone.
fact.zh: 据估计，全球可开采的磷酸盐储量有三分之二仅在摩洛哥。

ety.en: From Greek phōsphoros, 'light-bearer'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 phōsphoros，意为“带来光的”

sen.us: Plants need phosphorus to grow strong roots.
sen.uk: Plants need phosphorus to grow strong roots.
sen.zh: 植物需要磷来长出强壮的根。

traps.why_en: The stress is on the first syllable, FOS-fuh-rus, and the second 'o' is weak, not a full 'or' sound.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第一音节 FOS，第二个 o 要弱读，不要读成完整的 or。

fact.en: Sulfur is the tenth most abundant element by mass in the universe and the fifth most common on Earth.
fact.zh: 按质量计，硫在宇宙中丰度排第十，在地球上排第五。

sen.us: Our teacher showed us a bright yellow piece of sulfur.
sen.uk: Our teacher showed us a bright yellow piece of sulphur.
sen.zh: 老师给我们看了一块亮黄色的硫。

fact.en: Your white blood cells make tiny amounts of chlorine to fight bacteria.
fact.zh: 你的白细胞会产生微量氯气来对抗细菌。

ety.en: From Ancient Greek chlōros, 'pale green', for the gas's colour
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 chlōros，意为“淡绿色”，取自它的颜色。

sen.us: The swimming pool smelled strongly of chlorine today.
sen.uk: The swimming pool smelled strongly of chlorine today.
sen.zh: 今天游泳池里的氯味很浓。

traps.why_en: Here ch sounds like k, as in KLOR-een, not like the ch in 'chair'.
traps.why_zh: 这里的 ch 读作 k，读 KLOR-een，不读 chair 里的 ch 音。

fact.en: Air holds about 23 times more argon than carbon dioxide.
fact.zh: 空气中氩的含量约是二氧化碳的23倍。

ety.en: From Ancient Greek argon, 'lazy' or 'inactive'
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 argon，意为“懒惰的、不活泼的”

sen.us: The light bulb is filled with argon gas.
sen.uk: The light bulb is filled with argon gas.
sen.zh: 这个灯泡里充满了氩气。

fact.en: Potassium is a metal so soft that you can easily cut it with a knife.
fact.zh: 钾是一种很软的金属，用小刀就能轻松切开。

ety.en: From English potash, 'pot ash': ash of burnt wood heated with water in a pot
ety.zh: 源自英语 potash，即放在锅里加水熬煮的草木灰

sen.us: Bananas are a good source of potassium.
sen.uk: Bananas are a good source of potassium.
sen.zh: 香蕉是钾的良好来源。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the second syllable: puh-TAS-ee-um.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第二个音节，读 puh-TAS-ee-um，不在开头。

traps.why_en: The symbol K comes from Latin kalium, but the English name is potassium.
traps.why_zh: 符号 K 来自拉丁语 kalium，但英语名称是 potassium。

fact.en: Corals, sea shells and pearls are mostly made of calcium carbonate.
fact.zh: 珊瑚、贝壳和珍珠主要由碳酸钙构成。

ety.en: From Latin calx, 'lime'
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 calx，意为“石灰”

sen.us: Milk has a lot of calcium for strong bones.
sen.uk: Milk has a lot of calcium for strong bones.
sen.zh: 牛奶含有大量钙，有助于骨骼强壮。

fact.en: Scandium is only the 50th most common element on Earth, but the 23rd in the Sun.
fact.zh: 钪在地球上仅排第50位，在太阳中却排第23位。

ety.en: From Latin Scandia, 'Scandinavia'
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 Scandia，意为“斯堪的纳维亚”

sen.us: Some light bike frames contain a little scandium.
sen.uk: Some light bike frames contain a little scandium.
sen.zh: 一些轻型自行车车架含有少量钪。

fact.en: Moon rocks brought back by Apollo 17 are about 12% titanium dioxide.
fact.zh: 阿波罗17号带回的月球岩石约12%是二氧化钛。

ety.en: Named after the Titans of Greek mythology
ety.zh: 以希腊神话中的泰坦神命名

sen.us: My new glasses have a light titanium frame.
sen.uk: My new glasses have a light titanium frame.
sen.zh: 我的新眼镜是轻巧的钛金属镜框。

traps.why_en: The first i sounds like 'tie' and the stress is on TAY: tie-TAY-nee-um.
traps.why_zh: 第一个 i 读作 tie 的音，重音在 TAY：tie-TAY-nee-um。

fact.en: Vanadium's first large-scale industrial use was in the steel alloy chassis of the Ford Model T.
fact.zh: 钒的第一个大规模工业用途，是用于福特T型车的钢合金底盘。

ety.en: From Old Norse Vanadís, another name for the goddess Freyja (beauty and fertility)
ety.zh: 源自古诺尔斯语 Vanadís，即象征美与生育的女神芙蕾雅的别名

sen.us: These strong tools are made with vanadium steel.
sen.uk: These strong tools are made with vanadium steel.
sen.zh: 这些结实的工具是用钒钢做的。

traps.why_en: The stressed 'a' in -na- is said like 'nay' (və-NAY-dee-əm), not 'nah', and the first 'a' is weak.
traps.why_zh: 重读音节 -na- 读作 "nay"（/neɪ/），不是 "nah"，第一个 a 要弱读。

fact.en: Polished chromium reflects almost 70% of visible light and almost 90% of infrared light.
fact.zh: 抛光的铬能反射近70%的可见光和近90%的红外光。

ety.en: From Greek chrōma, 'colour', because many of its compounds are brightly coloured
ety.zh: 源自希腊语chrōma，意为“颜色”，因其许多化合物颜色鲜艳

sen.us: The chromium on my bike shines like a mirror.
sen.uk: The chromium on my bike shines like a mirror.
sen.zh: 我自行车上的铬像镜子一样闪亮。

fact.en: About 80% of the world's known manganese resources are in South Africa.
fact.zh: 全球已知的锰资源约有80%位于南非。

ety.en: Italian physician Michele Mercati called magnesia nigra 'manganesa'; the metal isolated from it became 'manganese'.
ety.zh: 意大利医生梅尔卡蒂称magnesia nigra为manganesa，从中分离的金属后称manganese。

sen.us: Manganese helps make steel strong and hard.
sen.uk: Manganese helps make steel strong and hard.
sen.zh: 锰有助于让钢变得坚固耐磨。

traps.why_en: Manganese and magnesium look alike, so learners often say one when they mean the other.
traps.why_zh: 锰和镁的英文名很像，学习者常把两者混淆。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the first syllable, MANG-guh-neez, not on the last one.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第一个音节MANG，而不是最后一个音节。

fact.en: By mass, iron is the most common element on Earth, making up much of Earth's core.
fact.zh: 按质量计，铁是地球上最多的元素，地核大部分由铁构成。

sen.us: Spinach is a good source of iron.
sen.uk: Spinach is a good source of iron.
sen.zh: 菠菜是铁的良好来源。

traps.why_en: Iron is said EYE-ern (UK EYE-uhn); the o is not pronounced as a full vowel.
traps.why_zh: iron 读作 EYE-ern（英式 EYE-uhn），o 不读成完整元音。

fact.en: People have used cobalt to color glass since the Bronze Age.
fact.zh: 早在青铜时代，人们就用钴给玻璃着色。

ety.en: Possibly from German kobelt, the name 16th-century silver miners gave a nuisance type of ore
ety.zh: 可能源自德语 kobelt，16世纪银矿工给一种讨厌矿石起的名字

sen.us: My phone battery contains a small amount of cobalt.
sen.uk: My phone battery contains a small amount of cobalt.
sen.zh: 我的手机电池里含有少量的钴。

fact.en: Nickel is one of only four elements that are magnetic at about room temperature.
fact.zh: 镍是室温下具有铁磁性的仅有四种元素之一。

ety.en: From German Nickel, a mischievous sprite in miners' folklore
ety.zh: 源自德国矿工传说中的捣蛋小妖精 Nickel。

sen.us: My bike bell is shiny because it is covered in nickel.
sen.uk: My bike bell is shiny because it is covered in nickel.
sen.zh: 我的自行车铃很亮，因为它镀了一层镍。

fact.en: The biggest lump of pure copper ever found weighed 420 tonnes. It was found in Michigan in 1857.
fact.zh: 迄今发现的最大天然铜块重达420吨，1857年发现于美国密歇根。

ety.en: From Latin aes cyprium, 'metal of Cyprus'
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 aes cyprium，意为“塞浦路斯的金属”

sen.us: The wire inside this cable is made of copper.
sen.uk: The wire inside this cable is made of copper.
sen.zh: 这根电缆里的电线是铜做的。

fact.en: After iron, zinc is the most common trace metal in the human body.
fact.zh: 锌是人体内含量仅次于铁的微量金属。

ety.en: Probably from German Zinke, 'prong, tooth', named by Paracelsus
ety.zh: 可能源自德语 Zinke，意为“尖齿”，由帕拉塞尔苏斯命名。

sen.us: Sunscreen with zinc helps protect your skin at the beach.
sen.uk: Sunscreen with zinc helps protect your skin at the beach.
sen.zh: 含锌的防晒霜能在海边保护你的皮肤。

fact.en: Gallium melts in your hand, because body temperature is warmer than its melting point.
fact.zh: 镓的熔点低于体温，放在手里就会熔化。

ety.en: From Latin Gallia, 'Gaul', an old name for France
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 Gallia，意为“高卢”，即法国的古称。

sen.us: Our teacher showed us gallium melting in a warm cup.
sen.uk: Our teacher showed us gallium melting in a warm cup.
sen.zh: 老师给我们看了镓在温热的杯子里熔化。

fact.en: Like water, germanium expands as it freezes from a liquid, which few substances do.
fact.zh: 和水一样，锗从液态凝固时会膨胀，这样的物质很少。

ety.en: From Latin Germania, 'Germany', in honor of Winkler's homeland
ety.zh: 来自拉丁语 Germania，意为“德国”，以纪念温克勒的祖国。

sen.us: Our teacher showed us a small piece of germanium.
sen.uk: Our teacher showed us a small piece of germanium.
sen.zh: 老师给我们看了一小块锗。

traps.why_en: The g is soft /dʒ/ as in 'Germany', and the stress falls on the second syllable: jer-MAY-nee-um.
traps.why_zh: g 读软音 /dʒ/，同 Germany，重音在第二音节 MAY。

fact.en: During the Bronze Age, people melted arsenic with copper to make arsenical bronze.
fact.zh: 青铜时代，人们把砷和铜熔在一起，制成砷青铜。

ety.en: From Syriac zarnika, via Arabic al-zarnīḵ 'the orpiment', based on Persian zar, 'gold'
ety.zh: 源自叙利亚语 zarnika，经阿拉伯语“雌黄”，词根为波斯语 zar“金”

sen.us: Our chemistry teacher said arsenic is a very dangerous poison.
sen.uk: Our chemistry teacher said arsenic is a very dangerous poison.
sen.zh: 我们的化学老师说，砷是一种非常危险的毒药。

fact.en: In 1873, Willoughby Smith found that light changes how well grey selenium conducts electricity.
fact.zh: 1873年，威洛比·史密斯发现光会影响灰硒的导电性。

ety.en: Berzelius named it after the Moon, because it was similar to tellurium, named for the Earth
ety.zh: 贝采利乌斯以月亮命名它，因为它像以地球命名的碲

sen.us: Brazil nuts contain selenium, which our bodies need in small amounts.
sen.uk: Brazil nuts contain selenium, which our bodies need in small amounts.
sen.zh: 巴西坚果含有硒，我们的身体需要少量这种元素。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the second syllable, which has a long 'ee' sound: suh-LEE-nee-um.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第二个音节，读长音 ee：suh-LEE-nee-um。

fact.en: Bromine is a liquid at standard conditions; the only other element that is liquid is mercury.
fact.zh: 标准状况下溴是液体，另一种液态元素只有汞。

ety.en: From Greek βρῶμος (brōmos), 'stench'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 βρῶμος，意为“恶臭”

sen.us: Our teacher showed us bromine, a red-brown liquid.
sen.uk: Our teacher showed us bromine, a red-brown liquid.
sen.zh: 老师给我们看了溴，一种红棕色的液体。

traps.why_en: The ending -ine here sounds like 'meen', not like the word 'mine'.
traps.why_zh: 词尾 -ine 读作“meen”，不要读成 mine 的音。

fact.en: From 1960 to 1983, the official length of a metre was based on light from krypton.
fact.zh: 1960年至1983年，“米”的官方定义以氪发出的光为基准。

sen.us: Some camera flashes use krypton to make bright white light.
sen.uk: Some camera flashes use krypton to make bright white light.
sen.zh: 有些相机闪光灯用氪来发出明亮的白光。

fact.en: Some natural rubidium is radioactive, with a half-life over three times the universe's estimated age.
fact.zh: 天然铷中有28%带微弱放射性，半衰期超过宇宙估计年龄的三倍。

ety.en: From Latin rubidus, 'deep red'
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 rubidus，意为“深红色”

sen.us: Our teacher said rubidium is used in some atomic clocks.
sen.uk: Our teacher said rubidium is used in some atomic clocks.
sen.zh: 老师说一些原子钟里会用到铷。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the second syllable: roo-BID-ee-um, not on the first or third.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第二个音节 BID 上，不要重读第一个或第三个音节。

fact.en: At the peak of TV tube production, up to 75% of US strontium went into TV screen glass.
fact.zh: 显像管电视鼎盛时期，美国多达75%的锶用于屏幕玻璃。

ety.en: Named after Strontian, a Scottish village where it was found in the ores of lead mines
ety.zh: 得名于苏格兰村庄斯特朗申，人们在当地铅矿的矿石中发现了它

sen.us: My chemistry teacher showed us strontium burning with a red flame.
sen.uk: My chemistry teacher showed us strontium burning with a red flame.
sen.zh: 化学老师给我们演示了锶燃烧时发出的红色火焰。

fact.en: Until the early 1920s, yttrium's chemical symbol was Yt, not Y.
fact.zh: 直到20世纪20年代初，钇的化学符号还是Yt，而不是Y。

ety.en: Named after the mineral ytterbite, which was named after the village of Ytterby in Sweden
ety.zh: 得名于矿物ytterbite，该矿物以瑞典村庄于特比命名

sen.us: Yttrium helps the LED lights in our classroom glow.
sen.uk: Yttrium helps the LED lights in our classroom glow.
sen.zh: 钇让我们教室里的LED灯发光。

traps.why_en: The first Y is a vowel, so the name starts with the sound /ɪ/ (IT-ree-um), with no 'y' sound in front.
traps.why_zh: 开头的Y在这里是元音，读作/ɪ/（IT-ree-um），前面没有“y”的音。

fact.en: Zirconium alloys wrap nuclear fuel rods because they absorb very few neutrons.
fact.zh: 锆合金用来包裹核燃料棒，因为它几乎不吸收中子。

ety.en: From the mineral zircon, related to Persian zargun, 'gold-like'
ety.zh: 来自矿物锆石，与波斯语zargun（“像金子”）有关

sen.us: The dentist used a zirconium crown on my back tooth.
sen.uk: The dentist used a zirconium crown on my back tooth.
sen.zh: 牙医给我的后牙装了一个锆牙冠。

fact.en: Of 44,500 tonnes of niobium mined in 2006, an estimated 90% was used in high-grade structural steel.
fact.zh: 2006年开采的44500吨铌中，估计约90%用于高级结构钢。

ety.en: From Greek myth: Niobe, daughter of Tantalus, the namesake of tantalum
ety.zh: 源自希腊神话：坦塔罗斯之女尼俄伯（钽名源自坦塔罗斯）

sen.us: Niobium makes the steel in gas pipelines stronger.
sen.uk: Niobium makes the steel in gas pipelines stronger.
sen.zh: 铌让天然气管道里的钢更坚固。

traps.why_en: The first 'i' is said like 'eye' (nye-OH-bee-um), not 'ee' as in pinyin 'ni'.
traps.why_zh: 开头的 i 读作 /aɪ/（像 eye），不要按拼音读成 ni。

fact.en: About 80% of the world's molybdenum is used in steel alloys.
fact.zh: 全世界约80%的钼都用于钢合金。

ety.en: From Ancient Greek mólybdos, meaning 'lead'
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 mólybdos，意为“铅”。

sen.us: Our teacher said molybdenum makes steel much harder.
sen.uk: Our teacher said molybdenum makes steel much harder.
sen.zh: 老师说钼能让钢变得更硬。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the second syllable, mo-LIB-duh-num, and the 'e' is reduced to a weak 'uh'.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第二音节 mo-LIB，e 要弱读成 /ə/，不能读成 DEE。

traps.why_en: The 'y' is a short vowel /ɪ/ as in 'sit', not 'eye', and the 'd' must still be heard.
traps.why_zh: y 读短元音 /ɪ/（像 sit），不读 /aɪ/，d 音也不能漏掉。

fact.en: Technetium is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive.
fact.zh: 锝是所有同位素都具有放射性的元素中最轻的一种。

ety.en: From a Greek word meaning 'artificial'; it was the first mainly artificial element made, in 1937
ety.zh: 源自希腊语，意为“人造的”；1937年成为第一种主要靠人工制得的元素

sen.us: Doctors use technetium to take pictures of our bones.
sen.uk: Doctors use technetium to take pictures of our bones.
sen.zh: 医生用锝来拍摄我们骨骼的影像。

traps.why_en: The 'ch' is a hard /k/ sound, the stress is on 'NEE', and 'ti' sounds like 'sh': tek-NEE-shee-um.
traps.why_zh: ch 读作 /k/，重音在 NEE 上，ti 读作“诗”音：tek-NEE-shee-um。

fact.en: Many fountain pen nibs are tipped with a ruthenium alloy.
fact.zh: 许多钢笔的笔尖尖端是用钌合金制成的。

ety.en: From Latin Ruthenia, a name for Russia, chosen to honour Russia
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 Ruthenia，即“俄罗斯”，以纪念俄罗斯

sen.us: Our teacher said ruthenium makes some pen tips very hard.
sen.uk: Our teacher said ruthenium makes some pen tips very hard.
sen.zh: 老师说钌能让一些笔尖变得非常坚硬。

traps.why_en: The th is a soft /θ/ sound and the stress falls on the second syllable: roo-THEE-nee-um.
traps.why_zh: th 要发咬舌音 /θ/，重音在第二音节 THEE，不要读成 t 或 s。

fact.en: Tiny traces of rhodium have been measured in some potatoes.
fact.zh: 人们在一些土豆中检测到了微量的铑。

ety.en: From Greek rhodon, meaning 'rose'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 rhodon，意为“玫瑰”

sen.us: Her white gold ring has a shiny rhodium coating.
sen.uk: Her white gold ring has a shiny rhodium coating.
sen.zh: 她的白金戒指有一层闪亮的铑镀层。

fact.en: Some professional concert flutes are made from palladium.
fact.zh: 一些专业音乐会长笛是用钯制成的。

ety.en: Named after the asteroid Pallas, itself named from a title of the Greek goddess Athena
ety.zh: 得名于小行星帕拉斯，其名源自希腊女神雅典娜的称号

sen.us: My uncle bought a small palladium coin as a gift.
sen.uk: My uncle bought a small palladium coin as a gift.
sen.zh: 我叔叔买了一枚小钯金币当礼物。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the second syllable LAY: puh-LAY-dee-um.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第二音节 LAY，读作 puh-LAY-dee-um，不要重读第一或第三音节。

fact.en: In ancient Egypt, silver once cost more than gold.
fact.zh: 在古埃及，银曾经比金子还贵。

ety.en: From Old English seolfor (also siolfor), the word for this metal
ety.zh: 源自古英语 seolfor（也写作 siolfor），指这种金属

sen.us: She wore a silver necklace to the school party.
sen.uk: She wore a silver necklace to the school party.
sen.zh: 她戴着一条银项链去参加学校聚会。

fact.en: In 2022, tests of 28 dark chocolate brands sold in the US found cadmium in all of them.
fact.zh: 2022年，对美国在售的28个黑巧克力品牌检测，全部含有镉。

ety.en: From Latin cadmia, Greek kadmeia, 'calamine', named after Cadmus, the mythical founder of Thebes
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语cadmia、希腊语kadmeia（炉甘石），得名于底比斯创建者卡德摩斯

sen.us: My teacher said cadmium is a toxic metal.
sen.uk: My teacher said cadmium is a toxic metal.
sen.zh: 我的老师说镉是一种有毒的金属。

fact.en: One of indium's discoverers was color-blind, so his assistant had to spot the colored spectral lines.
fact.zh: 铟的发现者之一是色盲，只好请助手帮他辨认光谱线的颜色。

ety.en: From Latin indicum, 'of India', after the indigo color seen in its spectrum
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 indicum（“印度的”），因光谱中的靛蓝色得名

sen.us: Indium helps the touch screen on my phone work.
sen.uk: Indium helps the touch screen on my phone work.
sen.zh: 铟让我手机的触摸屏能够正常工作。

fact.en: When you bend a bar of tin, it makes a sound called the 'tin cry'.
fact.zh: 弯曲锡条时，它会发出一种声音，叫作“锡鸣”。

ety.en: From Proto-Germanic *tin-om; German Zinn and Dutch tin share the same root
ety.zh: 源自原始日耳曼语 *tin-om，与德语 Zinn 同源

sen.us: We collected tin cans for the school recycling project.
sen.uk: We collected tin cans for the school recycling project.
sen.zh: 我们为学校的回收项目收集了锡罐。

fact.en: An artifact said to be part of a vase made of antimony, from about 3000 BC, was found in present-day Iraq.
fact.zh: 一件据称是锑制花瓶残片的文物，约公元前3000年，出土于今伊拉克。

ety.en: From medieval Latin antimonium; where that word comes from is uncertain
ety.zh: 源自中世纪拉丁语 antimonium，该词本身来源尚不确定

sen.us: Old car batteries contain lead mixed with antimony.
sen.uk: Old car batteries contain lead mixed with antimony.
sen.zh: 旧汽车电池里含有掺了锑的铅。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the first syllable, AN-ti-moh-nee, not the second.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第一个音节 AN，而不是第二个音节。

fact.en: People exposed to tellurium can have breath that smells like garlic.
fact.zh: 接触过碲的人，呼出的气会带有大蒜味。

ety.en: From Latin tellus, meaning 'earth'
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 tellus，意为“大地”

sen.us: Some solar panels use a thin layer containing tellurium.
sen.uk: Some solar panels use a thin layer containing tellurium.
sen.zh: 有些太阳能电池板使用含碲的薄层。

fact.en: Not getting enough iodine affects about two billion people around the world.
fact.zh: 全球约有二十亿人受到缺碘的影响。

ety.en: From Ancient Greek Ιώδης (iodes), meaning 'violet'
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 Ιώδης，意为“紫色”

sen.us: The nurse put some iodine on my cut knee.
sen.uk: The nurse put some iodine on my cut knee.
sen.zh: 护士在我擦伤的膝盖上涂了一些碘酒。

traps.why_en: It starts with the sound 'eye' and the stress is on it: EYE-uh-dine (US) or EYE-uh-deen (UK).
traps.why_zh: 开头读作“爱”，重音在第一个音节，不读成“哟”。

fact.en: When frozen solid, xenon is denser than granite rock.
fact.zh: 固态氙的密度比花岗岩还大。

ety.en: From Greek xénos, 'foreigner', 'stranger' or 'guest'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 xénos，意为“外来者、陌生人、客人”

sen.us: Our camera flash uses xenon gas to make bright light.
sen.uk: Our camera flash uses xenon gas to make bright light.
sen.zh: 我们的相机闪光灯用氙气发出强光。

traps.why_en: An x at the start of an English word is said /z/, so xenon begins like 'zee'.
traps.why_zh: 英语词首的 x 读 /z/，所以 xenon 开头像 “zee”，不读 /ks/。

fact.en: Since 1967, the official length of one second has been defined using caesium atoms.
fact.zh: 自1967年起，“一秒”的长度就是用铯原子来定义的。

ety.en: From Latin caesius, chosen for the bright blue lines in its spectrum
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 caesius，因其光谱中明亮的蓝线而得名

sen.us: Atomic clocks use cesium to keep very exact time.
sen.uk: Atomic clocks use caesium to keep very exact time.
sen.zh: 原子钟用铯来保持非常精确的时间。

traps.why_en: The 'ae' is said like 'ee', the c is /s/ and the s is /z/: SEE-zee-um.
traps.why_zh: ae 读作 “ee”，c 读 /s/，s 读 /z/，应读 SEE-zee-um。

fact.en: Barium compounds are added to fireworks to give them a green colour.
fact.zh: 烟花里加入钡的化合物，可以让烟花呈现绿色。

ety.en: From the alchemical word "baryta", from Greek βαρὺς, meaning 'heavy'
ety.zh: 源自炼金术用语"baryta"，来自希腊语βαρὺς，意为"重"。

sen.us: The doctor gave me a barium drink before my X-ray.
sen.uk: The doctor gave me a barium drink before my X-ray.
sen.zh: 拍X光之前，医生让我喝了一杯钡剂。

traps.why_en: The first 'a' sounds like the 'air' in 'hair' (BAIR-ee-um), not the open 'ah' in 'car'.
traps.why_zh: 开头的a读作hair里的"air"音，而不是car里的"啊"音。

fact.en: Lanthanum is almost three times as abundant as lead in the Earth's crust.
fact.zh: 镧在地壳中的含量几乎是铅的三倍。

ety.en: From ancient Greek lanthanein, meaning 'to lie hidden'
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 lanthanein，意为“隐藏”。

sen.us: Lighter flints contain a metal called lanthanum.
sen.uk: Lighter flints contain a metal called lanthanum.
sen.zh: 打火机的火石里含有一种叫镧的金属。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the first syllable (LAN-thuh-num), and 'th' is the soft /θ/ sound, not a 't'.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第一个音节 LAN，th 要读成咬舌音 /θ/，不是 t。

fact.en: Most white LED lights get their white glow from a cerium-containing coating over blue LEDs.
fact.zh: 大多数白光LED靠蓝光LED加含铈的荧光粉发出白光。

ety.en: Named after the asteroid Ceres, found two years earlier
ety.zh: 以两年前发现的小行星谷神星（Ceres）命名

sen.us: Lighter flints spark because they contain cerium.
sen.uk: Lighter flints spark because they contain cerium.
sen.zh: 打火机的火石能打出火花，是因为里面含铈。

fact.en: Silicate crystals doped with praseodymium ions slowed a light pulse to a few hundred meters per second.
fact.zh: 掺有镨离子的硅酸盐晶体曾把光脉冲减慢到每秒几百米。

ety.en: From Ancient Greek πράσινος, 'leek-green', and δίδυμος, 'twin'
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 πράσινος（韭绿色）和 δίδυμος（双胞胎）

sen.us: Our teacher showed us green glass made with praseodymium.
sen.uk: Our teacher showed us green glass made with praseodymium.
sen.zh: 老师给我们看了用镨制成的绿色玻璃。

traps.why_en: The y is a short 'i' as in 'dim', the s sounds like z, and the main stress falls on DIM: pray-zee-oh-DIM-ee-um.
traps.why_zh: y 读短音 /ɪ/（像 dim），s 读 /z/，重音在 DIM 上：pray-zee-oh-DIM-ee-um。

traps.why_en: In this long name the stress does not move to the end; keep it on DIM.
traps.why_zh: 这个长单词的重音不在词尾，要落在 DIM 上。

fact.en: Glass containing neodymium can look like a different color under different kinds of light.
fact.zh: 含钕的玻璃在不同灯光下会呈现不同的颜色。

ety.en: From Greek neos, 'new', + didymos, 'twin'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 neos“新”和 didymos“双胞胎”

sen.us: My headphones use a tiny neodymium magnet.
sen.uk: My headphones use a tiny neodymium magnet.
sen.zh: 我的耳机里有一块小小的钕磁铁。

fact.en: At any moment, only about 500–600 grams of promethium exist naturally in all of Earth's crust.
fact.zh: 任何时刻，整个地壳中天然存在的钷只有约500–600克。

ety.en: From Greek myth: Prometheus, the Titan who stole fire and gave it to humans
ety.zh: 源自希腊神话中为人类盗取火种的泰坦神普罗米修斯

sen.us: Promethium was once used in glowing paint for signal lights.
sen.uk: Promethium was once used in glowing paint for signal lights.
sen.zh: 钷曾被用在信号灯的发光涂料里。

traps.why_en: The th is the tongue-between-teeth /θ/ sound, not s: pro-MEE-thee-um.
traps.why_zh: th 要发咬舌音 /θ/，不能读成 s：pro-MEE-thee-um。

fact.en: Samarium was the first chemical element ever named after a person.
fact.zh: 钐是第一个以人名命名的化学元素。

ety.en: From the mineral samarskite, named after Russian Vassili Samarsky-Bykhovets
ety.zh: 源自矿物铌钇矿（samarskite），以俄国人萨马尔斯基命名

sen.us: Samarium magnets still work well when they get very hot.
sen.uk: Samarium magnets still work well when they get very hot.
sen.zh: 钐磁铁在温度很高时依然能正常工作。

fact.en: Tiny traces of europium make some natural fluorite crystals glow bright blue.
fact.zh: 微量的铕能让某些天然萤石发出明亮的蓝色荧光。

ety.en: Named after the continent of Europe
ety.zh: 以欧洲（Europe）命名

sen.us: Europium helps old TV screens show bright red.
sen.uk: Europium helps old TV screens show bright red.
sen.zh: 铕帮助老式电视屏幕显示鲜艳的红色。

traps.why_en: Unlike 'Europe', the stress falls on the second syllable: yoo-ROH-pee-um.
traps.why_zh: 和 Europe 不同，重音在第二音节：yoo-ROH-pee-um。

fact.en: Below about 20 °C, gadolinium becomes magnetic and is pulled by magnets more strongly than nickel.
fact.zh: 钆在约20°C以下具有铁磁性，被磁铁吸引得比镍还强。

ety.en: From the mineral gadolinite, itself named after the Finnish chemist Johan Gadolin
ety.zh: 源自矿物硅铍钇矿（gadolinite），该矿以芬兰化学家加多林命名

sen.us: Doctors sometimes use gadolinium to make MRI scans clearer.
sen.uk: Doctors sometimes use gadolinium to make MRI scans clearer.
sen.zh: 医生有时用钆让核磁共振图像更清晰。

fact.en: Terbium has been found in the air of KELT-9b, a very hot planet outside our Solar System.
fact.zh: 人们在太阳系外的炽热行星KELT-9b的大气中探测到了铽。

ety.en: Named after Ytterby, a village in Sweden
ety.zh: 以瑞典村庄伊特比（Ytterby）命名

sen.us: Terbium helps some lamps give off bright green light.
sen.uk: Terbium helps some lamps give off bright green light.
sen.zh: 铽能帮助一些灯发出明亮的绿光。

fact.en: No mineral has yet been found in which dysprosium is the main rare earth.
fact.zh: 至今还没有发现以镝为主要稀土成分的矿物。

ety.en: From Greek dysprositos, 'hard to get'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 dysprositos，意为“难以得到”

sen.us: Our teacher said dysprosium helps make magnets for electric cars.
sen.uk: Our teacher said dysprosium helps make magnets for electric cars.
sen.zh: 我们老师说镝有助于制造电动汽车用的磁铁。

traps.why_en: The y is a short 'i' as in 'dis', and the s in -sium sounds like /z/: dis-PROH-zee-um.
traps.why_zh: y 读短音 /ɪ/，像 dis；-sium 中的 s 读 /z/，不读 /s/。

fact.en: In 2017, IBM stored one bit of computer data on a single holmium atom.
fact.zh: 2017年，IBM把一比特数据存储在了单个钬原子上。

ety.en: From Latin Holmia, the name for the city of Stockholm
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语 Holmia，即斯德哥尔摩的拉丁名

sen.us: Doctors use a holmium laser to break up kidney stones.
sen.uk: Doctors use a holmium laser to break up kidney stones.
sen.zh: 医生用钬激光击碎肾结石。

fact.en: A Swiss scientist mistakenly switched the names of the two oxides erbia and terbia.
fact.zh: 一位瑞士科学家曾把氧化物“铒土”和“铽土”的名字弄反了。

ety.en: Named for Ytterby, a village in Sweden
ety.zh: 得名于瑞典的一个村庄伊特比（Ytterby）

sen.us: Our teacher said erbium helps send internet signals through cables.
sen.uk: Our teacher said erbium helps send internet signals through cables.
sen.zh: 老师说铒有助于通过线缆传送网络信号。

fact.en: Thulium's symbol was first Tu, but it was changed to Tm to avoid confusion with tungsten.
fact.zh: 铥的符号最初是Tu，后来改为Tm，以免与钨混淆。

ety.en: From Thule, an Ancient Greek place name linked with Scandinavia or Iceland
ety.zh: 源自古希腊地名Thule，与斯堪的纳维亚或冰岛相关

sen.us: Our teacher said thulium is a rare metal used in lasers.
sen.uk: Our teacher said thulium is a rare metal used in lasers.
sen.zh: 我们老师说铥是一种用于激光器的稀有金属。

traps.why_en: The 'th' is the soft /θ/ sound with the tongue between the teeth, not /s/ or /t/.
traps.why_zh: th要读成咬舌音/θ/，不要读成/s/或/t/。

fact.en: Four elements, ytterbium, yttrium, terbium and erbium, are all named after one village.
fact.zh: 镱、钇、铽、铒四种元素都以同一个村庄命名。

ety.en: Named after Ytterby, a village in Sweden
ety.zh: 以瑞典村庄伊特比（Ytterby）命名

sen.us: Can you find ytterbium on the periodic table?
sen.uk: Can you find ytterbium on the periodic table?
sen.zh: 你能在元素周期表上找到镱吗？

traps.why_en: The first 'y' is a vowel /ɪ/, not a 'y' consonant, and stress falls on the second syllable: ih-TUR-bee-um.
traps.why_zh: 开头的 y 读元音 /ɪ/，重音在第二个音节 TUR。

fact.en: Lutetium costs about US$10,000 per kilogram, about a quarter of the price of gold.
fact.zh: 镥每公斤约一万美元，大约是黄金价格的四分之一。

ety.en: From Latin Lutetia, the Latin name for Paris
ety.zh: 源自拉丁语Lutetia，即巴黎的拉丁名

sen.us: Lutetium is the last element in the lanthanide row.
sen.uk: Lutetium is the last element in the lanthanide row.
sen.zh: 镥是镧系那一行的最后一个元素。

fact.en: Pure hafnium is not toxic, but it can catch fire by itself in air.
fact.zh: 纯铪无毒，但在空气中能自己着火。

ety.en: From Hafnia, the Latin name for Copenhagen, where it was discovered
ety.zh: 源自哥本哈根的拉丁名Hafnia，铪在那里被发现

sen.us: My brother learned that hafnium was named after Copenhagen.
sen.uk: My brother learned that hafnium was named after Copenhagen.
sen.zh: 我哥哥了解到铪是以哥本哈根命名的。

fact.en: Before tungsten took over, tantalum wires were used as light bulb filaments.
fact.zh: 在钨取而代之之前，灯泡灯丝曾用钽丝制成。

ety.en: Named after Tantalus, a figure in Greek mythology
ety.zh: 以希腊神话人物坦塔罗斯命名

sen.us: Some phones contain a little tantalum inside.
sen.uk: Some phones contain a little tantalum inside.
sen.zh: 有些手机里含有少量钽。

fact.en: Tungsten has the highest melting point of all known elements, at 3422 °C.
fact.zh: 钨是所有已知元素中熔点最高的，达3422°C。

ety.en: The name tungsten was the old Swedish name for scheelite and other minerals of similar density.
ety.zh: “tungsten”曾是瑞典语对白钨矿及密度相近矿物的旧称。

sen.us: The old light bulb has a thin tungsten wire inside.
sen.uk: The old light bulb has a thin tungsten wire inside.
sen.zh: 这个旧灯泡里有一根细细的钨丝。

traps.why_en: The first u sounds like the u in 'sun', and the second syllable is weak: TUNG-stən, not a full 'sten'.
traps.why_zh: 第一个u读作sun里的/ʌ/，第二音节要弱读成/stən/，不要读成完整的“斯坦”。

fact.en: Rhenium was first found in 1908, but its discoverer thought it was a different element.
fact.zh: 铼早在1908年就被发现，但发现者误以为它是另一种元素。

ety.en: From Rhenus, meaning the river Rhine in Europe
ety.zh: 源自Rhenus，意为欧洲的莱茵河。

sen.us: Rhenium helps jet engines stay strong at very high temperatures.
sen.uk: Rhenium helps jet engines stay strong at very high temperatures.
sen.zh: 铼能让喷气发动机在极高温度下保持坚固。

fact.en: Osmium is the densest stable element, and it is also one of the rarest in Earth's crust.
fact.zh: 锇是密度最大的稳定元素，在地壳中也极为稀少。

ety.en: From Greek osme, 'a smell', after the strong smell of its oxide
ety.zh: 源自希腊语osme，意为“气味”，因其氧化物气味刺鼻。

sen.us: Some expensive fountain pens have osmium alloy on their tips.
sen.uk: Some expensive fountain pens have osmium alloy on their tips.
sen.zh: 一些昂贵的钢笔笔尖上有锇合金。

fact.en: Unusually high iridium in a clay layer led to the idea that an impact ended the non-bird dinosaurs.
fact.zh: 黏土层中铱含量异常高，引出了天体撞击导致非鸟恐龙灭绝的假说。

ety.en: From Greek iris, 'rainbow', for the various colors of its compounds
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 iris（彩虹），指其化合物的多种颜色

sen.us: My dad's car uses iridium spark plugs that last a long time.
sen.uk: My dad's car uses iridium spark plugs that last a long time.
sen.zh: 我爸爸的车用的是铱火花塞，能用很久。

traps.why_en: Because of the word 'iris', learners often start with 'eye', but iridium starts with a short 'i' and is stressed on the second syllable: ih-RID-ee-um.
traps.why_zh: 受 iris 影响容易读成“艾”，其实开头是短音 /ɪ/，重音在第二音节：ih-RID-ee-um。

fact.en: One rock layer, the Merensky Reef, holds around 75% of the world's known platinum.
fact.zh: 仅一个岩层——梅伦斯基矿层，就含有世界已知铂的约75%。

ety.en: From Spanish platina, a diminutive of "silver" ('little silver')
ety.zh: 源自西班牙语 platina，是“银”的指小词，意为“小银”。

sen.us: Her wedding ring is made of platinum.
sen.uk: Her wedding ring is made of platinum.
sen.zh: 她的结婚戒指是铂金做的。

traps.why_en: The stress goes on the first syllable, PLAT-in-um, and the middle i is short and weak.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第一个音节 PLAT，中间的 i 要读得短而轻，不读长音 ee。

fact.en: A single gram of gold can be beaten into a sheet of 1 square metre.
fact.zh: 仅一克金就能被捶打成一平方米的薄片。

ety.en: From Proto-Germanic *gulþą, which comes from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃-
ety.zh: 源自原始日耳曼语 *gulþą，再上溯至原始印欧语 *ǵʰelh₃-

sen.us: My grandmother wears a thin gold ring every day.
sen.uk: My grandmother wears a thin gold ring every day.
sen.zh: 我奶奶每天都戴着一枚细细的金戒指。

fact.en: In 2020, China was the top producer of mercury, providing 88% of world output (2,200 of 2,500 tonnes).
fact.zh: 2020年，中国是最大的汞生产国，产量占全球88%（2500吨中的2200吨）。

ety.en: From the planet Mercury: the modern English name comes from the planet's name.
ety.zh: 现代英文名 mercury 来自行星“水星”（Mercury）。

sen.us: The old thermometer in our classroom had mercury inside it.
sen.uk: The old thermometer in our classroom had mercury inside it.
sen.zh: 我们教室里那支旧温度计里面装有汞。

fact.en: Thallium poisoning usually makes a person's hair fall out.
fact.zh: 铊中毒通常会导致头发脱落。

ety.en: From Greek thallos, 'a green shoot or twig'
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 thallos，意为“嫩绿的枝芽”

sen.us: Our teacher said thallium was once used in rat poison.
sen.uk: Our teacher said thallium was once used in rat poison.
sen.zh: 老师说铊以前曾被用在老鼠药里。

traps.why_en: The 'th' is /θ/, with the tongue between the teeth, not an /s/ sound.
traps.why_zh: th 要读成咬舌音 /θ/，不能读成 /s/。

fact.en: Pencil 'leads' in wooden pencils have never been made from lead.
fact.zh: 木头铅笔里的“铅芯”从来都不是用铅做的。

ety.en: Of Germanic origin; comes from Middle English leed and Old English lēad
ety.zh: 源自日耳曼语，来自中古英语 leed 和古英语 lēad。

sen.us: My old fishing weights are made of lead.
sen.uk: My old fishing weights are made of lead.
sen.zh: 我那些旧钓鱼坠子是用铅做的。

traps.why_en: The metal is said /led/ like 'red'; 'leed' is the verb meaning 'to guide'.
traps.why_zh: 金属铅读 /led/，和 red 押韵；读成 leed 是动词“带领”。

fact.en: Unusually, bismuth expands as it turns solid, which made it useful for casting printing type.
fact.zh: 铋凝固时会膨胀，这很少见，因此曾被用来铸造印刷铅字。

ety.en: Possibly from German Bismuth or Wismut, perhaps related to Old High German hwiz, 'white'
ety.zh: 可能源自德语 Wismut，或与古高地德语 hwiz（“白”）有关

sen.us: Some stomach medicine contains a little bismuth.
sen.uk: Some stomach medicine contains a little bismuth.
sen.zh: 有些胃药含有少量铋。

traps.why_en: The s is said as /z/ (BIZ-muth), and the final th is /θ/, not /s/.
traps.why_zh: s 要读成 /z/（BIZ-muth），结尾 th 是咬舌音 /θ/，不是 /s/。

fact.en: Only about 100 grams of polonium are produced each year, practically all of it in Russia.
fact.zh: 全世界每年只生产约100克钋，几乎全部产自俄罗斯。

ety.en: Named after Poland (Polonia), Marie Curie's native land
ety.zh: 以居里夫人的祖国波兰（Polonia）命名

sen.us: Marie Curie named polonium after her home country, Poland.
sen.uk: Marie Curie named polonium after her home country, Poland.
sen.zh: 居里夫人用她的祖国波兰为钋命名。

fact.en: No one has ever seen solid astatine: any visible piece would boil away from its own radioactive heat.
fact.zh: 从没人见过固态砹：任何肉眼可见的一块都会被自身放射热瞬间汽化。

ety.en: From Ancient Greek astatos (ἄστατος), 'unstable'
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 astatos（ἄστατος），意为“不稳定的”

sen.us: Our teacher said astatine is the rarest element in nature.
sen.uk: Our teacher said astatine is the rarest element in nature.
sen.zh: 老师说砹是自然界中最稀有的元素。

fact.en: Radon is heavier than air, so it can collect in basements under people's homes.
fact.zh: 氡比空气重，所以会积聚在住宅下方的地下室里。

sen.us: We tested our basement for radon last winter.
sen.uk: We tested our basement for radon last winter.
sen.zh: 去年冬天我们检测了地下室里的氡。

traps.why_en: The first 'a' sounds like 'ray', so say RAY-don, not the pinyin-style 'ra'.
traps.why_zh: 首字母 a 读作“ray”的音，应读 RAY-don，不要按拼音读成“ra”。

fact.en: At any moment, only about one ounce of francium exists in the whole of Earth's crust.
fact.zh: 任何时刻，整个地壳中的钫总共只有约一盎司（约28克）。

ety.en: Named after France, where Marguerite Perey discovered it in 1939
ety.zh: 以法国命名，1939年佩雷在法国发现了它

sen.us: Francium is named after the country France.
sen.uk: Francium is named after the country France.
sen.zh: 钫是以法国这个国家命名的。

fact.en: Pure radium is silvery-white, but in air it reacts with nitrogen and forms a black surface layer.
fact.zh: 纯镭呈银白色，但在空气中会与氮反应，表面形成一层黑色物质。

ety.en: From French radium, formed in Modern Latin from radius, 'ray'
ety.zh: 源自法语 radium，由现代拉丁语 radius（射线）构成

sen.us: Old watches used radium paint to glow in the dark.
sen.uk: Old watches used radium paint to glow in the dark.
sen.zh: 旧手表用镭涂料在黑暗中发光。

traps.why_en: The first 'a' sounds like the 'a' in 'ray' (RAY-dee-um), not the short 'a' in 'rad'.
traps.why_zh: 第一个 a 读作 ray 里的 /eɪ/，不是 rad 里的短音 /æ/。

fact.en: Actinium glows pale blue in the dark, because its radiation makes the air around it light up.
fact.zh: 锕在黑暗中发出淡蓝光，因为它的辐射让周围空气发光。

ety.en: From Ancient Greek aktis, aktinos, 'beam' or 'ray'
ety.zh: 源自古希腊语 aktis（aktinos），意为“光束、射线”

sen.us: In class, we learned that actinium glows blue in the dark.
sen.uk: In class, we learned that actinium glows blue in the dark.
sen.zh: 课上我们学到锕在黑暗中会发出蓝光。

fact.en: Thorium is estimated to be over three times as abundant as uranium in the Earth's crust.
fact.zh: 据估计，钍在地壳中的含量是铀的三倍多。

ety.en: Named after Thor, the Norse god of thunder and war
ety.zh: 得名于北欧神话中的雷神与战神托尔（Thor）

sen.us: Old camping lamps sometimes used thorium in their gas mantles.
sen.uk: Old camping lamps sometimes used thorium in their gas mantles.
sen.zh: 旧式露营灯的纱罩有时会用到钍。

traps.why_en: The 'th' is /θ/, made with the tongue between the teeth, not an 's' or 't' sound.
traps.why_zh: th 读 /θ/，舌尖要放在上下齿之间，不能读成 s 或 t。

fact.en: Protactinium is one of the rarest and most expensive elements found in nature.
fact.zh: 镤是自然界中最稀有、最昂贵的元素之一。

ety.en: From Greek prôtos, 'first, before', + actinium: the parent of actinium
ety.zh: 源自希腊语 prôtos（“最先”）加锕，意为“锕之母”

sen.us: Our teacher said protactinium is too rare to use outside labs.
sen.uk: Our teacher said protactinium is too rare to use outside labs.
sen.zh: 老师说镤太稀有了，只能在实验室里用。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the third syllable: pro-tak-TIN-ee-um.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第三个音节上：pro-tak-TIN-ee-um。

fact.en: Uranium is about 40 times more common in Earth's crust than silver.
fact.zh: 铀在地壳中的含量大约是银的40倍。

ety.en: Named by Klaproth after Uranus, a planet that had only recently been discovered
ety.zh: 克拉普罗特以当时新发现的天王星为其命名

sen.us: Some power stations use uranium to make electricity.
sen.uk: Some power stations use uranium to make electricity.
sen.zh: 有些发电站用铀来发电。

traps.why_en: The stressed 'a' sounds like 'ay' in 'rain' (yoo-RAY-nee-um), not like pinyin 'ra'.
traps.why_zh: 重读的 a 要读成 rain 里的 /eɪ/，不是拼音“ra”的音。

fact.en: Neptunium is used to make plutonium-238, which is used to provide electricity for spacecraft.
fact.zh: 镎可用来制造钚-238，而钚-238用于为航天器供电。

ety.en: Named after Neptune, the planet beyond Uranus in the Solar System; uranium is named after Uranus.
ety.zh: 得名于太阳系中位于天王星之外的海王星；铀则以天王星命名。

sen.us: Our chemistry teacher said neptunium was first made in 1940.
sen.uk: Our chemistry teacher said neptunium was first made in 1940.
sen.zh: 我们的化学老师说，镎是在1940年首次被制造出来的。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the second syllable, nep-TOO-nee-um, not on the first syllable as in the planet name Neptune.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第二个音节 nep-TOO-nee-um，不要像行星名 Neptune 那样重读第一个音节。

fact.en: Plutonium has the highest atomic number of any element found in nature.
fact.zh: 钚是自然界中原子序数最高的元素。

ety.en: Named after Pluto, which was then thought of as a planet
ety.zh: 以当时被视为行星的冥王星命名

sen.us: Some spacecraft get their power from plutonium.
sen.uk: Some spacecraft get their power from plutonium.
sen.zh: 有些航天器靠钚来供电。

fact.en: Americium is widely used in smoke detectors.
fact.zh: 镅被广泛用于烟雾探测器。

ety.en: Named after the Americas, matching europium, the element above it
ety.zh: 仿照其上方的铕，以美洲命名

sen.us: The smoke alarm in our kitchen contains a little americium.
sen.uk: The smoke alarm in our kitchen contains a little americium.
sen.zh: 我们厨房的烟雾报警器里含有一点镅。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on 'ri' and 'ci' sounds like 'sh': am-uh-RISH-ee-um.
traps.why_zh: 重音在 ri 上，ci 读作“sh”：am-uh-RISH-ee-um。

fact.en: A scientist first revealed curium's discovery on a children's radio quiz show.
fact.zh: 锔的发现最早是一位科学家在儿童广播问答节目里透露的。

ety.en: Named after the scientists Marie and Pierre Curie, known for their research on radioactivity
ety.zh: 以研究放射性的科学家玛丽·居里和皮埃尔·居里命名

sen.us: Our teacher said curium was named after Marie and Pierre Curie.
sen.uk: Our teacher said curium was named after Marie and Pierre Curie.
sen.zh: 老师说锔是以玛丽·居里和皮埃尔·居里的名字命名的。

fact.en: Just over one gram of berkelium has been produced in the United States since 1967.
fact.zh: 自1967年以来，美国只生产了一克多一点的锫。

ety.en: From English place name Berkeley: named after the city of Berkeley, California
ety.zh: 源自英语地名Berkeley，以美国加州伯克利市命名

sen.us: Our chemistry teacher told us that berkelium is very rare.
sen.uk: Our chemistry teacher told us that berkelium is very rare.
sen.zh: 我们的化学老师告诉我们，锫非常稀有。

fact.en: Element 118, oganesson, was made by hitting californium-249 atoms with calcium-48 ions.
fact.zh: 118号元素鿫是用钙-48离子轰击锎-249原子合成的。

ety.en: Named after the university and the U.S. state of California
ety.zh: 以那所大学和美国加利福尼亚州命名

sen.us: Our teacher said californium was named after a US state.
sen.uk: Our teacher said californium was named after a US state.
sen.zh: 老师说锎是以美国的一个州命名的。

fact.en: Einsteinium is so radioactive that a sample gives off a visible glow by itself.
fact.zh: 锿的放射性极强，样品自己就会发出肉眼可见的光。

sen.us: My brother laughed when he heard that einsteinium is a real element.
sen.uk: My brother laughed when he heard that einsteinium is a real element.
sen.zh: 我哥哥听说锿是一种真实存在的元素时笑了。

traps.why_en: Learners keep Einstein's first-syllable stress, but the element is stressed on the second syllable: ine-STY-nee-um.
traps.why_zh: 学习者常沿用Einstein的首音节重音，但元素名重音在第二音节：ine-STY-nee-um。

fact.en: Fermium was discovered in 1952 in the debris of the first detonation test of a hydrogen bomb.
fact.zh: 镄于1952年在首次氢弹引爆试验的残骸中被发现。

ety.en: Named after Enrico Fermi, one of the pioneers of nuclear physics.
ety.zh: 以核物理先驱之一恩里科·费米的名字命名。

sen.us: Fermium was named after a famous scientist, our teacher said.
sen.uk: Fermium was named after a famous scientist, our teacher said.
sen.zh: 老师说，镄是以一位著名科学家的名字命名的。

fact.en: Mendelevium-256 was the first isotope of any element to be synthesized one atom at a time.
fact.zh: 钔-256是第一个被一个原子一个原子地合成出来的同位素。

ety.en: Named after Dmitri Mendeleev, the father of the periodic table
ety.zh: 以"元素周期表之父"德米特里·门捷列夫的名字命名

sen.us: Mendelevium is named after the man who made the periodic table.
sen.uk: Mendelevium is named after the man who made the periodic table.
sen.zh: 钔是以制定元素周期表的那个人命名的。

traps.why_en: The stress falls on the third syllable, men-de-LEE-vee-um, and the 'e' there is a long 'ee'.
traps.why_zh: 重音在第三个音节 LEE 上，读作 men-de-LEE-vee-um，不是 DEL。

fact.en: A Soviet team got credit for finding nobelium, but it kept the name Swedish scientists chose.
fact.zh: 锘的发现归功于苏联团队，却保留了瑞典人起的名字。

ety.en: Named after Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite
ety.zh: 以炸药发明者阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔命名

sen.us: Nobelium is element 102 on our classroom periodic table.
sen.uk: Nobelium is element 102 on our classroom periodic table.
sen.zh: 锘是我们教室元素周期表上的第102号元素。

fact.en: The first lawrencium atoms were reportedly made by hitting a three-milligram californium target with boron.
fact.zh: 据报道，最早的铹原子是用硼原子核轰击三毫克锎靶制得的。

sen.us: Our chemistry teacher said lawrencium is made in particle accelerators.
sen.uk: Our chemistry teacher said lawrencium is made in particle accelerators.
sen.zh: 我们的化学老师说，铹是在粒子加速器里制造出来的。

traps.why_en: The name Lawrence is stressed on its first syllable, but lawrencium moves the stress to REN: law-REN-see-um.
traps.why_zh: 人名 Lawrence 重音在第一个音节，但 lawrencium 的重音移到 REN 上。

fact.en: Books in the Soviet Bloc once officially called element 104 "kurchatovium".
fact.zh: 苏联阵营的书籍曾把104号元素正式称为“𬬻”的别名“库尔恰托夫元素”。

ety.en: Named after New Zealand physicist Ernest Rutherford, the "father" of nuclear physics
ety.zh: 以“核物理之父”、新西兰物理学家卢瑟福命名

sen.us: Rutherfordium is too rare for any school lab to have.
sen.uk: Rutherfordium is too rare for any school lab to have.
sen.zh: 𬬻太稀有了，任何学校实验室都不可能有。

traps.why_en: The th is a voiced /ð/ (tongue between teeth), not s or z; say ruh-ther-FOR-dee-um.
traps.why_zh: th 要发咬舌的浊音 /ð/，不要读成 s 或 z。

fact.en: JINR first proposed the name bohrium, then changed it to nielsbohrium to avoid confusion with boron.
fact.zh: JINR最初提议叫bohrium，后改为nielsbohrium，以免与硼混淆。

ety.en: Named in 1997 after the town of Dubna, the site of the JINR
ety.zh: 1997年以JINR所在地杜布纳镇命名

sen.us: In chemistry class, we learned that dubnium is made in labs.
sen.uk: In chemistry class, we learned that dubnium is made in labs.
sen.zh: 在化学课上，我们了解到𬭊是在实验室里制造的。

fact.en: It is one of only two elements named after a living person at the time of naming; the other is oganesson.
fact.zh: 𬭳是仅有的两种以命名时在世者命名的元素之一，另一种是鿫。

ety.en: Named after the American nuclear chemist Glenn T. Seaborg
ety.zh: 以美国核化学家格伦·T·西博格的名字命名

sen.us: Our teacher said seaborgium is named after a scientist.
sen.uk: Our teacher said seaborgium is named after a scientist.
sen.zh: 老师说𬭳是以一位科学家的名字命名的。

fact.en: Even the most stable known isotope of bohrium has a half-life of only about 2.4 minutes.
fact.zh: 即使是𬭛最稳定的已知同位素，半衰期也只有约2.4分钟。

ety.en: Named after the Danish physicist Niels Bohr
ety.zh: 以丹麦物理学家尼尔斯·玻尔的名字命名

sen.us: Our teacher said bohrium is not found in nature.
sen.uk: Our teacher said bohrium is not found in nature.
sen.zh: 老师说𬭛在自然界中不存在。

fact.en: Hassium behaves like a heavier osmium, reacting readily with oxygen to form a volatile tetroxide.
fact.zh: 𬭶的化学行为像更重的锇，易与氧反应生成易挥发的四氧化物。

ety.en: Named by GSI after the German state of Hesse, home to the facility
ety.zh: 由GSI以德国黑森州命名，该研究机构就位于黑森州

sen.us: Hassium was first made in a lab in Germany.
sen.uk: Hassium was first made in a lab in Germany.
sen.zh: 𬭶最早是在德国的一个实验室里制造出来的。

fact.en: Meitnerium is the only element named solely after a non-mythical woman.
fact.zh: 鿏是唯一一个只以一位真实女性命名的元素。

sen.us: Our teacher said meitnerium was named after a woman scientist.
sen.uk: Our teacher said meitnerium was named after a woman scientist.
sen.zh: 老师说鿏是以一位女科学家的名字命名的。

fact.en: Its discoverers also thought about naming it wixhausium, after Wixhausen, a suburb of Darmstadt.
fact.zh: 发现团队曾考虑以达姆施塔特郊区维克斯豪森命名为wixhausium。

ety.en: Named after Darmstadt, the German city where the element was discovered
ety.zh: 得名于发现该元素的德国城市达姆施塔特

sen.us: Darmstadtium was named after a city in Germany.
sen.uk: Darmstadtium was named after a city in Germany.
sen.zh: 𫟼是以德国的一座城市命名的。

fact.en: Only a few atoms of roentgenium have ever been made, and it has no practical use.
fact.zh: 人类只造出过极少量的𬬭原子，它没有任何实际用途。

ety.en: Named after German physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, who discovered X-rays
ety.zh: 以发现X射线的德国物理学家伦琴命名

sen.us: Roentgenium is named after the scientist who discovered X-rays.
sen.uk: Roentgenium is named after the scientist who discovered X-rays.
sen.zh: 𬬭是以发现X射线的科学家命名的。

fact.en: Copernicium is so volatile that it is possibly a gas or a liquid at standard temperature and pressure.
fact.zh: 鿔极易挥发，在标准温度和压力下可能是气体或易挥发的液体。

ety.en: Named after the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus, on his 537th anniversary
ety.zh: 以天文学家尼古拉·哥白尼的名字命名，时值其537周年纪念

sen.us: Copernicium was named after a famous astronomer.
sen.uk: Copernicium was named after a famous astronomer.
sen.zh: 鿔是以一位著名天文学家的名字命名的。

fact.en: Its most stable known form, nihonium-286, has a half-life of only about 10 seconds.
fact.zh: 它最稳定的已知同位素鿭-286，半衰期只有约10秒。

ety.en: From Japanese: one of the two Japanese pronunciations of the name of Japan
ety.zh: 源自日语：日本国名的两种日语读音之一

sen.us: Nihonium is element 113 on our classroom periodic table.
sen.uk: Nihonium is element 113 on our classroom periodic table.
sen.zh: 鿭是我们教室元素周期表上的第113号元素。

fact.en: Flerovium is very volatile and may even be a gas at standard temperature and pressure.
fact.zh: 𫓧挥发性很强，在标准温度和压力下甚至可能是气体。

ety.en: Named after the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions in Dubna, Russia
ety.zh: 以俄罗斯杜布纳的弗廖罗夫核反应实验室命名

sen.us: Our teacher said flerovium is named after a Russian lab.
sen.uk: Our teacher said flerovium is named after a Russian lab.
sen.zh: 老师说𫓧是以一个俄罗斯实验室命名的。

fact.en: Its most stable known isotope, moscovium-290, has a half-life of only 0.65 seconds.
fact.zh: 已知最稳定的同位素镆-290，半衰期只有0.65秒。

ety.en: Named after the Moscow Oblast, in which the JINR is situated.
ety.zh: 以莫斯科州命名，JINR就位于该州。

sen.us: Moscovium is element 115 on our classroom periodic table.
sen.uk: Moscovium is element 115 on our classroom periodic table.
sen.zh: 镆是我们教室元素周期表上的第115号元素。

fact.en: The Dubna team first wanted to name element 116 moscovium, but that name went to element 115 instead.
fact.zh: 杜布纳团队起初想把116号元素命名为“莫斯科”元素，此名后来给了115号元素。

ety.en: Named after the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in the city of Livermore, California, US
ety.zh: 以美国加州利弗莫尔市的劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室命名

sen.us: Our teacher said livermorium was named after a lab in California.
sen.uk: Our teacher said livermorium was named after a lab in California.
sen.zh: 老师说𫟷是以加州的一个实验室命名的。

fact.en: The target used to discover it traveled over the Atlantic Ocean five times in a few days.
fact.zh: 用于发现它的靶材在几天内五次飞越大西洋。

ety.en: Named after the US state or region of Tennessee, where key research institutions in its discovery are located
ety.zh: 以美国田纳西州命名，参与发现它的关键研究机构都在那里。

sen.us: Our teacher said Tennessine is named after a US state.
sen.uk: Our teacher said Tennessine is named after a US state.
sen.zh: 老师说鿬是以美国的一个州命名的。

fact.en: Theory predicts it would be a solid at room temperature, unlike the other noble gases.
fact.zh: 理论预测它在室温下是固体，与其他稀有气体不同。

ety.en: Named after the nuclear physicist Yuri Oganessian
ety.zh: 以核物理学家尤里·奥加涅相的名字命名

sen.us: Oganesson is the last element on the periodic table.
sen.uk: Oganesson is the last element on the periodic table.
sen.zh: 鿫是元素周期表上的最后一个元素。
